item.title: FIRED HENDERSONVILLE POLICE CAPTAIN DENIES MISCONDUCT CALLS ALLEGATIONS MISLEADING
item.description: A captain with the Hendersonville Police Department has issued a 24-page public statement after he was fired following allegations of "misuse of off-duty employment." On Feb. 5, 2026, Hendersonville city council officials announced Captain Kenneth Hipps was terminated from his position in January. item.title: HENDERSONVILLE FIRE DEPARTMENT CELEBRATES CHIEF MILLER'S RETIREMENT AND THE PROMOTION OF DEPUTY CHIEF WARD
item.description: The Hendersonville Fire Department formally recognized the retirement of Chief D. item.title: HENDERSONVILLE ADDS TRANSPORTATION BOND REFERENDUM ON BALLOT FOR PRIMARY ELECTION
item.description: The City of Hendersonville has announced that voters will vote on a Transportation General Obligation Bond referendum during the primary election. According to a news release, if the referendum is approved, it would authorize the city to issue up to $10 million in General Obligation bonds to help fund transportation infrastructure improvements. item.title: PERSIST OF HENDERSON COUNTY HOLDS MEMORIAL FOR LIVES LOST IN IMMIGRATION CRACKDOWN
item.description: Protests against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement are continuing across the United States, with many taking place in western North Carolina alone. On Saturday, Feb. 7, Persist of Henderson County organized a memorial for the lives lost during the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, including Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti.
